rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: They take waraʾ as what lies ahead of the man: Hell is in front of him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: يريد أمامه جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waraʾ can mean behind or ahead because its basic sense is what is concealed from someone; unseen ahead can be described like unseen behind.
rows.anchor: ووراء يكون لخلف وقدام، وإنما معناه ما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة وابن السكيت وأبو الهيثم
rows.claim: They treat waraʾ as a word with opposite senses, meaning either behind or ahead.
rows.anchor: وهو قول أبي عبيدة (¬3)، وابن السكيت

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Any place can be behind or ahead from a viewpoint, so waraʾ may mean ahead; the verse about a king ahead of travelers illustrates it.
rows.anchor: قال أهل المعاني: وإنما جاز ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He gives a third sense, after: Hell follows the despair implied by the preceding statement, like the poet's claim that none has a destination after God.
rows.anchor: وذكر ابن الأنباري وجها ثالثا؛ وهو: أن وراء هاهنا بمعنى بعد

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He reads waraʾ as after: Hell will catch up with the condemned, as severe cold behind someone will reach him; Labid uses the word for old age that will come upon him.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {من ورائه جهنم} يعني بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣadīd is the liquid from a wound, mixed with blood and pus.
rows.anchor: الصديد في اللغة: ماء الجرح المختلط بالدم والقيح

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the drink as pus and blood issuing from adulterers private parts; al-Qurazi and al-Rabi share this view.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد صديد القيح والدم الذي يخرج من فروج الزناة

rows.speaker: قتادة والكلبي
rows.claim: They say the liquid comes from the unbeliever skin and flesh.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة والكلبي: هو ما يخرج من جلد الكافر ولحمه

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He construes the phrase as water possessing pus; the author says this conflicts with the description of the drink given to the righteous.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: تقديره: من ماء ذي صديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tajaraʿa describes taking a drink in successive, reluctant sips; Ibn Abbas glosses it as drinking under compulsion.
rows.anchor: فإذا تابع الجرع مرة بعد أخرى كالمتكاره، قيل: تجرعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary refers back to its earlier explanation of kada in the verse about lightning almost taking sight.
rows.anchor: ذكرنا معنى (كاد) عند قوله: {يكاد البرق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sāgha means that a drink passes smoothly down the throat; the cited verse of al-Farra uses the verb for a drink going down.
rows.anchor: ويقال: ساغ الشراب في الحلق، يسوغ سوغا، وأساغه الله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: His cited poem uses sāgha for a drink that goes down smoothly.
rows.anchor: وأنشد الفراء (¬6): وساغ لي الشراب وكنت قبلا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They say the condemned drink it in sips because of its bitterness, and treat kada as redundant, so the phrase means he cannot swallow it.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون في هذه الآية: يتحساه ويشربه بالجرع لا بمرة واحدة لمرارته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses the inability to swallow as not getting the drink down.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا يجيزه

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They read the phrase as swallowing only after delay; Arabic ما كدت أقوم can mean that one eventually stood after a delay, so kada is not redundant.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: معنى {ولا يكاد يسيغه}: بعد إبطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the darkness verse, the context already proves that the person did not see, so kada there can be an emphatic addition.
rows.anchor: جاز أن تكون صلة؛ لأنه قد قام الدليل عند وصف تكاثف الظلمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reference to the drink melting what is inside the stomach presupposes that some of it was swallowed; the repeated sipping also signals that some goes down, making total inability to swallow implausible.
rows.anchor: والدليل على الإساغة قوله: {يصهر به ما في بطونهم}

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He reconciles the wording by taking the negation to mean that the drinker cannot swallow all of the drink, although he swallows some.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: ذكره ابن الأنباري وهو أن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, swallowing can imply willing acceptance and relish; the unbeliever sips in disgust and cannot drink the liquid readily in one gulp.
rows.anchor: أن معنى الإساغة في اللغة: إجراء الشراب في الحلق على تقبل النفس واستطابة المشروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both explanations can preserve the commentators' redundant reading of kada, but the interpretation that does not make kada redundant is stronger.
rows.anchor: وقول من لم يجعل (يكاد) صلة أمثل

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: One analysis supplies an omitted word: the agony and distress of death reach him, since death itself cannot arrive while he remains alive.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن هذا من باب حذف المضاف؛ على معنى: ويأتيه هم الموت وألمه وكربه

rows.speaker: أبو بكر
rows.claim: A second analysis takes death as deathlike misery and affliction: the unbeliever is figuratively dead while still breathing, a sense also attributed to al-Akhfash.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول أبي بكر، وهو معنى قول الأخفش

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A report calls poverty the greatest death, supporting figurative use of death for severe misery.
rows.anchor: ورد في الحديث: "إن الفقر مكتوب عند الله الموت الأعظم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poet says that one who dies and rests is not truly dead, but the miserable living person is; the lines support the figurative sense.
rows.anchor:
قال الشاعر (¬4):
ليس من مات فاستراح بميت

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains that death reaches the condemned from every hair on his body.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد من كل شعرة في جسده

rows.speaker: الثوري
rows.claim: He says death comes from every vein; most commentators likewise take the places to be parts of the body.
rows.anchor: وقال الثوري: من كل عرق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In another report, death comes at him from every direction: right, left, above, below, front, and behind.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس في قوله من كل مكان: أي من كل جهة

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He takes waraʾ here to mean in front of the condemned on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد أمامه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He reads the next punishment as coming after the pus drink; Abu Ishaq and Abu Bakr prefer this sense and paraphrase it as what follows that ordeal.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: يقول من بعد الصديد عذاب غليظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thick punishment means pains joined together and multiplied, like a thick thing whose parts have accumulated; compare the description of great punishment.
rows.anchor: ومعنى غلظ العذاب: اتصال الآلام وكثرتها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He parses the nominative parable as introducing what is being recited to the audience, a construction also held by Sibawayh.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: هو مرفوع على معنى: وفيما يتلى عليكم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He supplies the omitted noun deeds: the deeds of those who disbelieve are like ashes. Arabic can place the more definite genitive first and state the described noun afterward.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: التقدير مثل أعمال الذين كفروا بربهم كرماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary refers to its fuller discussion of the several analyses under the parable of the Garden promised to the God-fearing.
rows.anchor: ذكرناها مستقصاة في قوله: {مثل الجنة التي وعد المتقون}

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: He defines ashes as the fine particles of burned charcoal, reduced to extremely fine dust.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: الرماد دقاق الفحم من حراقة النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb rāmada is also used of placing meat in ashes, as in the proverb about roasting meat and then putting it in ashes.
rows.anchor: ورمد اللحم، إذا ألقاه في الرماد

rows.speaker: ابن السكيت والزجاج
rows.claim: They explain ʿāṣif as a wind that blows strongly.
rows.anchor: قال ابن السكيت: عصفت الريح وأعصفت، فهي ريح عاصف

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says the adjective follows the grammatical case of day although it describes wind: a day may be called cold or hot because those conditions occur in it; Abu Ubayda cites a night described as sleeping for the same reason.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: جعل العصوف تابعا لليوم في إعرابه

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: He treats this as ordinary Arabic attribution, comparing the night and day being assigned actions or qualities that belong to what occurs in them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو حاتم: هذا من كلام العرب

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: His other parse supplies wind: a day fierce with wind, with the noun omitted because wind was mentioned earlier; he cites a poem that similarly omits sun after mentioning it.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: والوجه الآخر (¬3) أن يريد: في يوم عاصف الريح

rows.speaker: الزجاج وغيره
rows.claim: They explain the parable as the unbelievers' acts offered to God being null and useless because they associated others with Him, like ash scattered by wind.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج وغيره: تأويله أن كل ما تقرب به الذين كفروا إلى الله فمحبط

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the unbelievers will find no reward in the afterlife for what they did in this world.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد لا يجدون ثواب ما عملوا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses distant error as great loss: their deeds vanish like ashes, and the loss is distant from any hope of return.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد الخسران الكبير

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He glosses it as prolonged error, meaning the unbelievers' way is far from guidance and return.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي (¬4): الخطاء الطويل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ata's transmission, people means the polytheists and their wrongdoing means fabricating lies about God; the phrase about leaving no creature means no fabricator would remain.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد المشركين، {بظلمهم} قال: يريد بافترائهم على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, God would immediately punish the fabricators and clear the earth of them; the unintroduced pronoun in عليها refers to earth, clear from the mention of creatures living on it.
rows.anchor: والكناية في: {عليها} تعود إلى الأرض ولم يسبق لها ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With Ibn Abbas's interpretation, creature is restricted to a fabricator, whereas most other commentators understand all terrestrial creatures.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا التفسير الدابة تختص بالمفتري

rows.speaker: السدي عن أصحابه
rows.claim: They interpret the verse as drought withholding rain until every creature on earth perishes.
rows.anchor: روى السدي عن أصحابه في قوله: {ما ترك عليها من دابة} يقول لأقحط المطر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: He says human sin nearly caused even the dung beetle in its hole to perish.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن مسعود أنه قرأ

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He says this kind of destruction already occurred in Noah's time.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في هذه الآية: قد فعل ذلك زمان نوح

rows.speaker: أبو حمزة الثمالي
rows.claim: He says rain is withheld so that everything would perish, explaining how the sins of the polytheists could endanger terrestrial creatures.
rows.anchor: كما روى عن أبي حمزة الثمالي (¬5) أنه قال: يحبس المطر فيهلك كل شيء

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They explain that killing the fathers for disbelief would leave no children, emptying the earth; God delays punishment to an appointed term so people may reproduce.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: معنى الآية، أن الله تعالى لو أهلك الآباء بكفرهم لم يكن الأبناء

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the appointed term as the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: والأجل المسمى في هذه الآية: القيامة، في قول عطاء عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other commentators take the appointed term as the end of each lifespan, which the author considers closer because the polytheists are punished when their lives end.
rows.anchor: وفي قول الآخرين: يعني منتهى الأجل وانقضاء العمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that people neither delay nor advance an hour was explained earlier in the commentary on al-Aʿraf.
rows.anchor: وذكرنا معنى: {لا يستأخرون ساعة ولا يستقدمون} في سورة الأعراف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary refers to its explanation of ʿibra under the verse about lessons for people of insight.
rows.anchor: ذكرنا معنى العبرة في سورة آل عمران عند قوله: {لعبرة لأولي الأبصار}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With an open initial nūn, nusqīkum means We give you drink until you are satisfied; scripture uses this form for drinking by the mouth.
rows.anchor: من فتح النون (¬3) فحجته ظاهرة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He prefers the reading with a damma, as it conveys continuous, plentiful drinking; asqā commonly expresses providing a lasting drink.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيدة الضم وقال: لأنه شرب دائم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He explains the masculine pronoun in their bellies by treating anʿām as a collective-gender noun that can be masculine or feminine; another verse uses the feminine.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: الأنعام لفظه لفظ جمع، وهو اسم للجنس يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: He likewise treats anʿām, though shaped as a plural, as a masculine singular collective such as qawm or nafar.
rows.anchor: وهذا مذهب سيبويه، قال في ذكره إن الاسم الواحد يجيء على أفعال

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He says naʿam and anʿām are equivalent, so the masculine pronoun follows the masculine meaning naʿam; he supports such sense-based agreement with poetry.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: النعم والأنعام شيء واحد، فرجع التذكير إلى معنى النعم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: The cited rajaz line uses masculine agreement with naʿam, supporting the masculine form.
rows.anchor: والدليل على أن النعم مذكر قول الراجز

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He reads the pronoun as referring to what was mentioned, supplying an understood word such as animals.
rows.anchor: قال الكسائي: أراد مما في بطون ما ذكرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He cites a line about chicks with masculine agreement for their entrails, a parallel for masculine agreement with the collective livestock noun.
rows.anchor: مثل الفراخ نتقت حواصله (¬2)

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: Arabic can use masculine agreement for an understood generic thing: the sun is called this when it rises, and a gift sent by a woman is followed by the masculine verb when Solomon receives it.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: هذا فاش في القرآن وفي كلامهم

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: The line he recites about Afraʾ treats the feminine name with masculine agreement, illustrating generic masculine reference.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: وسمعت الكسائي ينشد ما هو أشد من هذا

rows.speaker: الأحمر
rows.claim: His line about Umm ʿAmmar supplies another example of masculine agreement with a feminine referent.
rows.anchor:
قال وأنشدنا الأحمر (¬4):
إذ (¬5)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples use an implied masculine generic such as thing or person; true feminine nouns still require feminine agreement in standard speech.
rows.anchor: فهذا التذكير في هذه الأشياء أشد منه في الأنعام

rows.speaker: المؤرج
rows.claim: He proposes that the pronoun points to omitted milk: the phrase means from the milk in their bellies, since not all livestock produce milk.
rows.anchor: وذهب المؤرج في هذا إلى وجه آخر

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He prefers and elaborates the implied-milk analysis: the general term includes animals without milk, so the phrase singles out the milk-bearing subset and omits milk because it is understood.
rows.anchor: واختار صاحب النظم هذا الوجه وزاده بيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farth is the dung or chyme of the stomach; Ibn Abbas identifies it as feed inside the stomach.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد العلف الذي يكون في الكرش

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In a report through al-Kalbi from Abu Salih, food settles in the stomach with dung below, blood above, and milk between; blood enters veins, milk the udder, and dung remains.
rows.anchor: وروى الكلبي عن أبي صالح عنه أنه قال: إذا استقر العلف في الكرش صار أسفله فرثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pure milk has no admixture of blood or dung; sāʾigh means that it passes easily and pleasantly through the throat.
rows.anchor: خالصا}: لا يشوبه الدم ولا الفرث، {سائغا للشاربين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transformation of one kind of fodder into several products inside an animal demonstrates the Creator's power and oneness to a reflective person.
rows.anchor: حيث جعل العلف وهو جنس واحد أنواعا في بطن الدابة

rows.speaker: أصحابنا
rows.claim: They infer that human semen is not impure merely because it is inside the body beside impurities, as milk emerges pure beside blood and dung; semen can remain pure even through a path of impurity.
rows.anchor: قال أصحابنا: وهذه الآية تدل على أن مني الآدمي لا يكون نجسا

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He supplies an omitted relative phrase: from the fruits of palms and grapes you take from them an intoxicant; otherwise the pronoun would need to be feminine plural.
rows.anchor: تأويل الآية: ولكم من ثمرات النخيل والأعناب ما تتخذون منه سكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic may omit ma and min, as in the cited verses.
rows.anchor: والعرب تضمر (ما) و (من)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grapes are coordinated with the fruits, not with palms; otherwise the phrase would oddly mean fruits of grapes rather than fruit and grapes.
rows.anchor: والأعناب عطف على الثمرات لا على النخيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In reports from Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Shahr ibn Hawshab, and ʿAmr ibn Sufyan, intoxicant means what is forbidden from the two fruits and good provision what is permitted; in Ata's report, it means intoxicating drink before wine was prohibited.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال: السكر ما حرم من ثمرتيهما، والرزق الحسن ما أحل من ثمرتيهما

rows.speaker: عامة المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify sakar as wine and good provision as lawful products such as vinegar, raisins, and dates; they say the verse preceded wine's prohibition in al-Maʾida.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول عامة المفسرين؛ قالوا: السكر هي الخمر بعينها

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They choose the lexical meaning wine for sakar; Jarir's line uses sakar in that sense.
rows.anchor: وهذا القول هو اختيار الفراء (¬2) والزجاج

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He alone says sakar means food, citing poetry where a speaker makes the nobles' reputations his food.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة بوحده: السكر: الطعام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He rejects the food interpretation as less fitting than wine and reads the poem as saying the speaker intoxicates himself with the nobles' reputations.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: هذا بالخمر أشبه منه بالطعام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Those who reason recognize God unique power, affirm His prophet, and become certain of reward and punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد عقلوا عن الله قدرته

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The opening means God created people when they were nothing, then takes them at the end of their lifespans.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: ولم تكونوا شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ardhal al-ʿumur is the worst and lowest age; related forms describe the lowly followers in Hud and al-Shuʿaraʾ, and a parallel appears in al-Tin.
rows.anchor: وهو أرداه وأوضعه

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi, transmitted by Asbat, glosses the lowest age as senility.
rows.anchor: روى أسباط عن السدي: {إلى أرذل العمر}

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He identifies the lowest age as old age.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: {أرذل العمر}: الهرم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He specifies ninety years as the lowest age.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: تسعون سنة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A report from Ali specifies seventy-five years as the lowest age.
rows.anchor: روي عن علي -رضي الله عنه- قال: {أرذل العمر}: خمس وسبعون سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person returns to a childlike condition, forgetting what he learned because of age; Ibn Abbas likens him to a child without reason.
rows.anchor: أي ليرجع إلى حال الطفولية بنسيان ما كان علم؛ للكبر

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He says the change from knowledge to ignorance demonstrates God's power just as death and life do.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: معنى قوله: {لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا}

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says this does not happen to Muslims: longer life increases their honor, intelligence, and knowledge with God; he connects this with the exception for believers in al-Tin.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: ليس هذا في المسلمين

rows.speaker: عاصم عن عكرمة
rows.claim: He says a person who recites the Quran will not reach an age where he knows nothing after knowledge; the exception for believers and righteous deeds is explained as Quran reciters.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا روى عاصم (¬1) عن عكرمة، قال: من قرأ القرآن

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God is knowing of what He has done to His allies and enemies, and powerful to do whatever He wills.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد بما صنع بأوليائه وأعدائه، {قدير}: على ما يريد

rows.speaker: المنهال بن عمرو
rows.claim: A woman sent her son to ask the Prophet for clothing; when she asked for his shirt, he gave it to him, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روى المنهال بن عمرو قال: بعثت امرأة إلى رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root ghalla means insertion or putting inside; Imru al-Qays uses it for an eyelash inserted into the eyelid.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة: معنى الغل: الإدخال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To embezzle from spoils is called ghalla because the stolen item is hidden in a sleeve; a hand in shackles is likewise described as inserted into iron.
rows.anchor: ومنه قولهم: غل في الغنيمة إذا خان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: They take a hand shackled to the neck as an image of stinginess and withholding God's due in alms and family ties.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون في قوله: {ولا تجعل يدك مغلولة إلى عنقك}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command means do not keep the hand completely closed against giving good.
rows.anchor: لا تمسك يدك عن البذل كل الإمساك

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He says Arabic favors describing the hand as habitually shackled rather than saying it was shackled in a single act; the verse forbids a settled habit of withholding, not restraint when restraint is appropriate.
rows.anchor: والعلة في هذا النظم؛ أن الفعل أقل من النعت، والنعت ألزم وأكثر من الفعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He takes the prohibition on opening the hand all the way as a warning against giving away all one's spending and gifts.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد في النفقة والعطية

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: They take it as a prohibition on wasteful spending, spending in disobedience, and spending on what is improper.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: يعني التبذير والإنفاق في معصية الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase has two interpretations: do not spend everything even in obedience, or do not squander money as Mujahid and Qatada explain.
rows.anchor: فحصل في قوله: {ولا تبسطها كل البسط} وجهان من التفسير

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He says the person ends up blaming himself and being blamed by others.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: تلوم نفسك وتلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses mahsūr as having nothing left.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ليس عندك شيء

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He glosses mahsūr as being left cut off and without support.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: مقطوعا بك

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Arabic calls a camel mahsūr when its journey is exhausted and its progress stops; the verb describes driving an animal until it can no longer continue.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول للبعير: هو محسور إذا انقطع سيره

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He says giving can exhaust and cut off the giver just as travel exhausts a camel; the root also means to use up everything someone has, as with an exhausted animal or eye.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن قتيبة: أي تحسرك العطية وتقطعك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He interprets mahsūr as regretful for what one has done, though the author notes that the usual active forms for regret are ḥasir or ḥasrān, not mahsūr.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة في قوله: {محسورا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening idh cannot attach to the preceding question because the youths' flight was long before the Prophet; it attaches to an omitted command, remember when they fled.
rows.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون متعلقا بما قبله على تقدير: أم حسبت إذ أوى الفتية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths went to the cave and made it their shelter; Ibn Abbas says they fled there.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {أوى الفتية إلى الكهف}: صاروا إليه وجعلوه مأواهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses their going to the cave as fleeing to it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد هربوا إلى الكهف)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After fleeing those pursuing them, the youths prayed for mercy, understood here as forgiveness and provision.
rows.anchor: لما هربوا عمن يطلبهم اشتغلوا بالدعاء والتضرع إلى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: They ask for mercy from God alone so that it will make them independent of everyone else.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريدون تغنينا بها عن جميع من سواك)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayyiʾ means set right or prepare; rushd and its related forms are the opposite of error.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وهيئ لنا} أي: أصلح

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He explains the prayer as asking for guidance to what brings one near to God and pleases Him; Ibn Abbas says to direct their deeds toward God's love.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي أرشدنا إلى ما يقرب منك ويزلف عندك)

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: They parse the request as having an omitted noun, a thing of right guidance; further omission yields the sense, prepare what will enable us to attain guidance.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل المعاني: (تقدير الآية: هيئ لنا من أمرنا ذا رشد)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They explain striking the ears as putting the youths to sleep.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: (معناه: أنمناهم)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He says God prevented them from hearing, since a sleeper wakes when he hears; Ibn Abbas describes it as striking their ears with sleep.
rows.anchor: قال أبو إسحاق: (أي منعناهم أن يسمعوا؛ لأن النائم إذا سمع انتبه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom depicts overpowering sleep blocking sounds from reaching their ears; the poet's image of earth struck with barriers illustrates such prevention.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: سددنا آذانهم بالنوم الغالب عن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cave phrase identifies where they slept, while counted years names the duration; numbering years implies a large quantity because small amounts need no counting.
rows.anchor: وذكر العدد هاهنا يفيد كثرة السنين

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They parse adadan as an adjective meaning counted years, with either an omitted noun or a passive verbal noun used as its object.
rows.anchor: أنه نعت للسنين. المعنى: سنين ذات عدد، أي معدودة، هذا قول الفراء، والزجاج

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He also allows adadan as an accusative cognate expression: We counted them with counting.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (ويجوز أن # ينتصب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: God raised the youths from their sleep, meaning He woke them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد من بعد نومهم)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They gloss li-naʿlama as so that We may see; the commentary refers to parallel discussions in al-Baqara and Al Imran.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {لنعلم} المفسرون يقولون في هذا: (لنرى)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayy is nominative as a subject with ahṣā as predicate, while the object of knowing is implicit in the story; it behaves like asking which person stood.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {أي الحزبين} الآية، {أي} رفع بأحصى على الابتداء والخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayy is interrogative and cannot be governed by a preceding word except through a preposition; the commentary will revisit the construction under Maryam.
rows.anchor: و {أي} من حروف الاستفهام فلا يعمل فيه

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He identifies the two parties as successive rulers of the city on one side and the cave youths on the other.
rows.anchor: فقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (الحزبين الملوك الذين تداولوا المدينة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says the two parties were groups from the youths' own people.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: (الحزبين من قوم الفتية)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He identifies the two parties as believers and unbelievers.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (يعني المؤمنين والكافرين)

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He transmits a view that two groups of Muslims in the youths' era disputed how long the youths remained in the cave; its adherents distinguish the earlier Muslims from converts who saw them.
rows.anchor: وحكى الفراء: (أن طائفتين من المسلمين في دهر أصحاب الكهف اختلفوا في مدة لبثهم)

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He says the youths' own dispute about their duration was the reason God raised them, while affirming that God already knows everything and no event causes Him to learn it.
rows.anchor: قال صاحب النظم: [(هذا ما قصه ربنا]

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author finds the reported explanations of the two parties unconvincing because none resolves the ambiguity.
rows.anchor: فهذا ما وجدته للمفسرين في هذه الآية، وهو غير مقنع، ولا كاف

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He says both parties were groups among the youths: some rejected the claim that they slept a day or part of a day, showing disagreement among them.
rows.anchor: والحزبان جميعا من أصحاب الكهف، أنهم قالوا هذا القول منكرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls this reading remote: the wording about knowing which party counted the duration does not naturally mean that God raised them to cause a dispute among themselves.
rows.anchor: هذا كلامه، وهو بعيد؛ لأنه يجعل معنى قوله:

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد وغيرهما
rows.claim: They understand the parties as believers and unbelievers from the youths' people, who disputed the duration; God raised the youths to clarify it.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكره المفسرون: قتادة، ومجاهد، وغيرهما: (ليعلم أي الحزبين

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He allows amadan either as a specification of ahsa or as the duration object of labithu.
rows.anchor: فقال الفراء: (ويكون نصبه على وجهين: إن شئت

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He similarly allows amadan as a specification governed by ahsa or as an object governed by labithu.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق نحو هذا سواء فقال: ({أمدا} منصوب على نوعين: وهو على التمييز إن شئت

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: He rejects the specification parse: ahsa is a past verb, not a regular comparative, and the duration is not the semantic subject expected for a specification; it is instead an object.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي: (إن انتصاب الأمد بالتمييز عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The youths refer to their contemporaries under Daqyanus, who worshipped idols as gods besides God.
rows.anchor: هذا من قول أصحاب الكهف، ويعنون الذين كانوا في زمان دقيانوس عبدوا الأصنام

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He takes ʿalayhim to mean against the worship of the idols, which requires supplying an omitted noun such as worship or adoption.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: (ومعنى {عليهم} أي على عبادة الآلهة)

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He reads the apparent challenge lولا يأتون as denial: they have no clear proof for their idols, since asking why they did not bring proof implies that they failed to do so.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب النظم: (ظاهر قوله: {لولا يأتون}، حث وسؤال، وتأويله نفي وإبطال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the rhetorical reading also requires supplying worship, the author prefers al-Zajjaj's reading because it preserves the apparent force of the words; the pronoun may refer either to the people or the idols.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان كذلك فالقول الأول أولى؛ لأنه لا يحتاج فيه إلى العدول عن ظاهر قوله

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He parses the command to take refuge in the cave as the response to idh, like an if-then construction; it means make the cave your home.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: (هذا جواب "إذ" كما تقول: إذ فعلت كذا فافعل كذا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yanshur means that God will spread His mercy over the youths.
rows.anchor: {ينشر لكم ربكم من رحمته} أي: يبسطها عليكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says God will ease their fear of the king and his oppression, bringing them relief, kindness, and gentleness.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يسهل عليكم ما خوفكم من الملك وظلمه

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He understands the promised mرفق as breakfast or food.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: (يعني غداء يأكلونه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others gloss mرفق as an exit; in general it is anything by which one gets help or comfort.
rows.anchor: وكل ما ارتفقت به فهو مرفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word has variants mرفق and مرفق in both the sense of a useful matter and the body's elbow; Medinan readers use the open-mim form.
rows.anchor: ويقال فيه أيضا: مرفق بفتح الميم وكسر الفاء، كقراءة أهل المدينة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He defines mرفق as what one uses for support, distinguishing the body's joint as mرفق.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: (المرفق: ما ارتفقت به

rows.speaker: الأخفش
rows.claim: He glosses mرفقا as a thing they can use, like maqṭaʿ.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش: ({مرفقا} أي: شيئا يرتفقون به

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: He explains the kasra reading as a lexicalized noun rather than a regular place or verbal noun; the open form can be a dialect variant of the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: (قوله: جعله اسما، أي: جعل المرفق اسما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Most Arabs use kasra in both the word for a helpful matter and the elbow, though some use fatha for both; the opening may distinguish the elbow.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء: (وأكثر العرب على كسر الميم

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: He prefers kasra for a useful matter and fatha for the elbow.
rows.anchor: وقال يونس: (الذي أختار المرفق في الأمر، والمرفق في اليد)

rows.speaker: الأصمعي وقطرب
rows.claim: Al-Asmaʿi recognizes only kasra for both senses, while Qutrub reports both pronunciations for both.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصمعي: (لا أعرف إلا الكسر فيهما)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address to the viewer is hypothetical: it means that if you saw the sun at sunrise, you would see it turn away from their cave.
rows.anchor: وليس أن من خوطب بهذا يرى ذلك، ولكن العادة في المخاطبة تكون على هذا النحو

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses tazāwar as moving away; in another report he says it tilts away from the youths.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {تزاور} قال ابن عباس: تتنحى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tazāwar means to lean or turn, paralleling tamāyal; a poem describing a horse uses tamāyal as evidence.
rows.anchor: ومعنى التزاور: التمايل من الزور والأزور

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة وابن عامر
rows.claim: The Kufans read the verb without the extra ta of the reciprocal form, while Ibn Amir reads tazawwar.
rows.anchor: وقراءة أهل الكوفة: بحذف تاء التفاعل، وقرأ ابن عامر: تزور

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: He objects that azwar is not used for leaning away, only for being withdrawn or contracted; Antara line about recoiling from a spear supports that sense.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: (لا يوضع في هذا المعنى إنما يقال: هو مزوز عني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jarir line about the palanquins turning away from a tree supports using the verb for the sun apparent turning aside.
rows.anchor: والذي حسن القراءة به قول جرير (¬1): وفي الأظعان عن طلح ازورار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhāt al-yamīn means toward the right; dhāt stands in for a directional noun, and al-Akhfash parses it as an adverb.
rows.anchor: {ذات اليمين}، أي: ناحية اليمين، فذات هاهنا صفة قامت مقام الموصوف

rows.speaker: الوالبي عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses taqriḍuhum as leaving them.
rows.anchor: قال الوالبي عن ابن عباس: (تذرهم)

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatada says the sun leaves them; Muqatil says it passes them by.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: (تدعهم) (¬5). وقال مقاتل: (تجاوزهم)

rows.speaker: الأخفش والزجاج وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: They explain the sun as turning away from the youths and leaving them; al-Kisaʾi says the verb means to pass a place by.
rows.anchor: وقال الأخفش، والزجاج، وأبو عبيدة: (تعدل عنهم وتتركهم)

rows.speaker: ذو الرمة
rows.claim: His line about riders passing mountain passes on their left illustrates taqriḍ as going past or bypassing.
rows.anchor: وأنشد قول ذي الرمة (¬1): إلى ظعن يقرضن أقواز مشرف

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: He says qarḍ can mean cutting or traversing a land; a traveler who passed a place on the left has bypassed it.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: (القرض في أشياء)

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He describes a cave in Roman territory oriented toward Banat Naʿsh: the sun passes the cave right at sunrise and its left at sunset without striking it.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: (يقول إذا طلعت الشمس مالت عن كهفهم ذات اليمين

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They say the cave was in a sunny, open place facing Banat Naʿsh, yet the sun path spared the youths from heat, exposure, and worn clothing.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون: (أعلم الله تعالى أنه ثواهم في مقناة

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: He infers that the sun never, or almost never, reached them, preserving their bodies.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي الفارسي: (إذا مالت الشمس عنهم إذا طلعت

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He rejects the explanation that their physical location alone blocked the sun; God withheld its approach, light, and heat by power as a sign.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (هذا التفسير ليس ببين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse sign is God power to keep the sun from reaching them, rather than their lying in a naturally shaded place.
rows.anchor: فلا تنالهم طالعة ولا غاربة، لا بكونهم في مكان لا تصيبه الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lay in a broad part of the cave where cool air and a breeze could reach them; faja means an open, spacious area.
rows.anchor: كانوا في متسع من الكهف، ينالهم فيه برد الريح، ونسيم الهوى

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He gives the plural forms of faja as fajawat and faja, and cites a report about moving quickly when one finds an open space.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة: (وجمعها فجوات)

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He glosses faja as a place extending broadly in width; Ibn Abbas calls it spaciousness.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: (الفجوة: المكان الذاهب)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sun turning and passing away from the cave are signs of God power and kindness to the youths.
rows.anchor: ذلك التزاور والقرض من دلائل قدرة الله ولطفه بأصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided the youths, and a person is guided only by God guidance; the example of misguidance is Daqyanus and his followers, who have no guiding patron.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى أن الله تعالى هو الذي تولى هداية أصحاب الكهف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is hypothetical like the earlier mention of seeing the sun: if one saw them, one would think they were awake.
rows.anchor: أي: لو رأيتهم لحسبتهم أيقاظا

rows.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة والزجاج
rows.claim: They give ayqāẓ as a plural form of ayqaẓ, yaqīẓ, and yaqẓān; Ruʾba verse uses the word.
rows.anchor: قا له الأخفمش، وأبو عبيدة، والزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ruqud means sleepers and is a verbal noun used collectively like bowing, sitting, and prostrating; calling it a plural of raqid is morphologically remote.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {وهم رقود} أي: نائمون، وهو مصدر سمي به

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He says they seemed awake because their eyes were open.
rows.anchor: وهم نيام) (¬3)؛ قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He explains their appearance as awake by their frequent turning from side to side, supported by the following statement that God turned them.
rows.anchor: وحكى أبو إسحاق: (لكثرة تقلبهم، يظن أنهم غير نيام

rows.speaker: أبو عياض
rows.claim: Qatada transmits that Abu Iyad said they were turned over twice each year; Abu Hurayra is also said to hold this view.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: (ذكر لنا أن أبا عياض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the turning prevented the earth from consuming their flesh and wearing their bodies away.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية عطاء: (لئلا تأكل الأرض لحومهم، ولا تبليهم)

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: In a report through Ibn Abi Najih, they slept on their right sides for nine years, then on their left for nine years.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد قال: (يمكثون رقودا على أيمانهم تسع سنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhāt is an adverb meaning on the side of the right, as in the earlier phrase about the sun direction.
rows.anchor: و {ذات} منصوبة على الظرف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: They say the youths fled their king by night, met a shepherd with a dog, and the shepherd followed them in faith with his dog.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وأكثر المفسرين: (هربوا ليلا من ملكهم، فمروا براع

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: He tells that the dog barked, was repeatedly driven off, then spoke of loving God beloved and offered to guard the youths while they slept.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: (مروا بكلب فنبح عليهم فطردوه

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: He says the dog was used for hunting.
rows.anchor: وقال عبيد بن عمير: (كان ذلك كلب صيدهم)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dog stretched both arms flat on the ground rather than drawing them inward; a Prophetic report prohibits spreading the forearms in prayer like a beast.
rows.anchor: أي: يلقيهما على الأرض مبسوطتين غير مقبوضتين

rows.speaker: الحديث
rows.claim: A Prophetic report forbids laying the forearms flat in prayer like a wild animal.
rows.anchor: ومنه الحديث في الصلاة: أنه نهى عن افتراش السبع

rows.speaker: الليث
rows.claim: He defines the forearm as extending from the elbow to the tip of the middle finger; Ibn al-Sikkit says the noun is feminine.
rows.anchor: قال الليث: (الذراع: من طرف المرفق إلى أطراف الأصبع الوسطى)

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: The active participle basit governs its object because the scene is presented as ongoing; if the action were simply past, it would lose the participle verbal force.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي: (لولا حكاية الحال لم يعمل اسم الفاعل في ذراعيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In reports through Ali and Ata, he glosses waṣīd as the forecourt; Mujahid and al-Dahhak, most exegetes, and most lexicographers agree.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس في رواية على وعطاء: (بالفناء)

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد عن الأحمر
rows.claim: Al-Ahmar glosses waṣīd as a courtyard or open space.
rows.anchor: روى أبو عبيد عن الأحمر (¬4): (الوصيد: الفناء)

rows.speaker: الزجاج وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj calls it the house or home forecourt; Abu Ubayda gives plural forms wasaʾid and waṣd.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج: (الوصيد: فناء البيت، وفناء الدار)

rows.speaker: يونس والأخفش والفراء
rows.claim: They treat waṣīd and aṣīd as dialect variants, like wakāf and ikāf.
rows.anchor: وقال يونس والأخفش والفراء: (الوصيد والأصيد لغتان، مثل

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: He assigns waṣīd to Tihama and aṣīd to Najd, and says the Quran was revealed in Tihama speech.
rows.anchor: وقال الكسائي: (أهل تهامة (¬3) يقولون: الوصيد

rows.speaker: السدي عن عكرمة عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: This report interprets waṣīd as the door.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: (الوصيد: الباب

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: He prefers door: being at the door means being in its vicinity.
rows.anchor: واختيار المبرد قال: ({بالوصيد} عند أهل اللغة: بالباب

rows.speaker: عطاء وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: Ata says threshold, and Ibn Qutayba prefers that sense because a closed door meets the threshold; the cave had no literal threshold, so the dog occupied its place, though waṣīd may also mean door.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: (الوصيد: عتبة الباب) (¬7)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The derivation from asada and awsada, to shut a door, supports door or sealed entrance; readings of the closed-door term correspond to aṣīd or waṣīd.
rows.anchor: ويقال: أصدت الباب، وأوصدته إذا أطبقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both door and courtyard readings work: a sealed cave entrance makes the dog at the door, while the area outside the cave mouth is its forecourt; Saʿid ibn Jubayr ground or dust likely means forecourt.
rows.anchor: فالذين قالوا: إنه الباب، وافق قولهم أصل اللفظ في اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ittalaʿa means to look over or appear above something, as in the verse about the speaker looking down and seeing his companion.
rows.anchor: أي: أشرفت عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lawallayta means turn away and flee; firāran is accusative as a verbal noun because the verb sense is fleeing.
rows.anchor: أي: لأدبرت وانقلبت منهم فرارا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: God filled a viewer with fear to prevent anyone from seeing the youths.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: (هو أن الله تعالى منعهم بالرعب لئلا يراهم أحد)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Another explanation says their very long hair and fingernails would frighten anyone who saw them.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (قيل في التفسير: إنهم طالت شعورهم جدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light reading of l-muliʾta is preferred because Arabs commonly say fear filled me, while the heavy form is little known; poems attest both forms.
rows.anchor: والاختيار التخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thus points back to God putting them to sleep, increasing their guidance, and turning them over; just as God did those things, He raised them.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى ما تقدم من قوله: {فضربنا على آذانهم}

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He describes their bodies as emerging from that sleep, which resembled death.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: (أجسامهم من تلك النومة التي تشبه الموت)

rows.speaker: أبو علي الجرجاني
rows.claim: The purpose was for the youths to question one another and disagree about how long they had stayed.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الجرجاني: (ليكون بينهم تساؤل وتنازع واختلاف في مدة لبثهم)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He takes the question to mean how long it had been since they entered the cave.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد كم لنا منذ دخلنا الكهف)

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They entered in the morning and woke late in the day, first estimating a day and then revising to part of a day after seeing the sun.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: (إنهم دخلوا الكهف غدوة، وبعثهم الله في آخر النهار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says their leader Tamlikha returned knowledge of their duration to God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يرد تمليخا رئيسهم رد علم ذلك إلى الله)

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Warq means silver whether or not it has been struck into coins; the report about Arfaja making a silver nose supports the broader sense.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: (الفضة كانت مضروبة دراهم أو لا)

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They record several vocalized forms of warq, with kasra on the first syllable the least preferred; silver may also be called riqqa.
rows.anchor: وورق، وورق، مثل كبد، وكبد، وكبد، ذكر ذلك الفراء والزجاج

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: He derives riqqa from wariqa, as ṣila and ʿida are derived forms.
rows.anchor: قال الأزهري: (أصله: ورقة، مثل: صلة وعدة)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The youths carried coins stamped with the image of the king from whose rule they had fled.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (وكانت معهم دراهم عليها صورة الملك الذي كان في زمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city was called Daqsus and is said to be the present-day Tarsus.
rows.anchor: ويعني بالمدينة: دقسوس، وهي مدينتهم، ويقال: هي اليوم طرسوس

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He interprets the best food as lawful slaughter; Saʿid ibn Jubayr agrees, and al-Farra prefers this because many townspeople were Zoroastrians while some believers hid their faith.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: (يريد: أحل الذبائح)

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: He says they sought the most lawful food because a tyrannical ruler oppressed people in food and markets; the messenger was told not to buy anything obtained by injustice or extortion.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد: (أيها أحل، وكان لهم ملك غشوم يظلم الناس في طعامهم وأسواقهم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He includes both explanations: the food was lawful either because it came from a believer slaughter or because it was free of theft; grammatically ayyu is subject, azka predicate, and taʿāman specification.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق القولين جميعا وقال: (الآية من باب حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He glosses walyatalattaf as acting in secrecy while entering the city and buying food; the word also means to inspect carefully and use a discreet plan.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد يكون ذلك في ستر وكتمان)

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He says the messenger must tell no city resident either about the youths or their location.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: (يريد لا يخبرن بكم، ولا بمكانكم أحدا من أهل المدينة)

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He interprets the warning as telling the messenger not to expose his companions if he himself is discovered.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (أي إن ظهر عليه فلا يوقعن إخوانه فيما يقع فيه)

rows.speaker: السدي وغيره
rows.claim: They say the envoy was bound by an oath that, if captured, he would lead the captors to the others rather than keep the martyrdom to himself; the author finds this more fitting than Abu Ishaq reading.
rows.anchor: فقد ذكر السدي وغيره: (أن الرسول خرج من عندهم وقد أخذ عليه المواثيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers Ibn Abbas meaning: the envoy should not voluntarily inform anyone, but if discovered should point the discoverer to his companions so they share the testimony.
rows.anchor: والمعنى ما قاله ابن عباس، أنه لا يتولى إعلام أحد

rows.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
rows.claim: Daqyanus sealed the cave, intending the youths to die of thirst and hunger there; two believers recorded their names, lineage, and story on lead inside a copper chest by the entrance for future believers to discover.
rows.anchor: إن الفتية لما هربوا من ملكهم دقيانوس ودخلوا الكهف، أمر دقيانوس بالكهف أن يسد عليهم

rows.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
rows.claim: Many generations later, the righteous king Tindusis faced a dispute about the Resurrection and prayed for a sign; God inspired a man to dismantle the cave entrance while building a sheep enclosure.
rows.anchor: وخلفت بعدهم قرون وملوك كثيرة، وملك أهل تلك

rows.speaker: العلماء بأخبار القدماء
rows.claim: God terror kept people from entering; the youths awoke after more than three hundred years, sent a companion for food, were discovered, and the king came with the townspeople to see them.
rows.anchor: وبعث الله الفتية من نومهم فجلسوا فرحين، وأرسلوا أحدهم ليطلب لهم طعاما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means God made the youths known and revealed them; the commentary also discusses the verb earlier in al-Maʾida.
rows.anchor: أي: أطلعنا وأظهرنا عليهم)، كذا قال المفسرون
